page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.16xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 server powered by custom 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processors, configured with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Managed by the AWS Nitro Hypervisor, the instance incorporates burstable CPU performance characteristics within the seventh-generation flex instance family. The hardware includes 128 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per thread. The processor architecture provides 105 MB of shared L3 cache alongside specialized instruction extensions, including Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions 512 (AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16). Network throughput features a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, while local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs are absent.

In synthetic and practical benchmark workloads, the c7i-flex.16xlarge demonstrates strong resource processing throughput across several multi-threaded vector and memory operations. PassMark CPU execution tests place extended instruction handling, encryption, and physics calculations in the top performance quartile. Read-side memory bandwidth reaches 4612.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 200.81 GB/sec for large blocks. The presence of hardware acceleration for AMX and AVX-512 contributes to strong prompt processing throughput for 135M, 7B, and 70B parameter language models. Additional strong benchmark outputs include software compilation via Clang, multithreaded Bzip3 decompression, Redis SET operations processing up to 69.84 million operations per second, and static web serving reaching 68.5 GB/sec throughput.

The burstable CPU allocation and flex profile provide a cost-efficient alternative to dedicated full-performance compute instances for workloads with variable utilization patterns. However, the lack of dedicated local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached block storage, and writing large memory blocks yields average bandwidth of 83.14 GB/sec. The 2 GB per vCPU ratio makes this configuration ideal for compute-intensive tasks with moderate memory footprints, such as software compilation, vector-accelerated text and image processing, web serving, database execution, and light CPU-based LLM inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.16xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 instance featuring 64 burstable vCPUs driven by 32 physical cores of a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Operating on the AWS Nitro Hypervisor, it includes 128 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, 105 MB of L3 cache, and network baseline throughput of 12 Gbps, while omitting local storage and GPUs. Hardware features include Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, delivering strong benchmark performance in extended vector instructions, software compilation, Redis SET operations, and CPU-based LLM inference. Read memory bandwidth reaches top-tier speeds for small and large cached blocks, though large block write operations exhibit average performance. The burstable CPU allocation provides qualitative cost advantages for bursty compute workloads. The c7i-flex.16xlarge is suited for software build pipelines, static web serving, high-throughput caching, and compute-heavy analytical data processing.
